determination_table_content.details:
MM Security Supplies Pty Ltd (MM Security) proposes to acquire the
business assets and goodwill of Micron Alarm Supplies Pty Ltd,
trading as Micron Security Products (Micron Security Products)
(the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, MM Security, is a wholly owned subsidiary of MML
Holdings Limited, a diversified Australian company which has
interests in businesses offering electronic security equipment as
well as other products.
MM Security operates several separately branded wholesale
businesses which source locally produced and imported electronic
security equipment, including CCTV systems, intrusion alarm
equipment, access control devices, intercom systems and related
electronic security equipment and accessories. MM Security has a
national footprint operating six separately branded wholesale
businesses.
The target, Micron Security Products, is an Australian importer and
wholesale supplier of electronic security equipment, including CCTV
systems, intrusion alarm equipment, intercom systems, access
control equipment and related accessories. Micron operates two
stores, in Seven Hills, Sydney and Hendra, Brisbane, and provides
online retailing nationally.

MM Security and Micron Security Products overlap in the supply of
wholesale electronic security equipment.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The increase in market share at the metropolitan or national
level resulting from the Acquisition is estimated to be low.
• The merged firm would continue to face competition from
multiple alternative wholesalers of electronic security
equipment, across the relevant geographic areas where the
Parties’ activities overlap. While some market participants
suggested the Acquisition would reduce customers’ choice of
suppliers, most customers of the Parties considered they would
continue to have access to a range of alternative suppliers post-
Acquisition.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

limited assets from Toll that comprise Toll Transport Pty Ltd’s (Toll)

Acquisition). The assets the subject of the Acquisition comprise
owned or leased equipment (trailers, prime movers and other

contracts, and two customer contracts.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has

The acquirer, Silk, is a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of DP World

contract logistics services. DPW, through its subsidiary DP World
Australia Ltd, operates international container terminals and
providers container stevedoring services at the Ports of Melbourne,
Botany, Brisbane and Fremantle.
Toll is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toll Holdings Pty Limited. Toll
operates a bulk logistics business offering specialised services for
the transportation of bulk products. The target business, Toll’s
plastics and glass bulk logistics business, provides warehousing,
and containerised and loose bulk transportation services to
customers in the plastics and glass industries, predominately in
Victoria (through the Ports of Melbourne, Botany, Brisbane, and
Kembla).

Both Silk and Toll’s plastics and glass bulk logistics business
operate in the supply of bulk containerised logistics services to
customers in Australia, including to customers requiring logistics
services for plastics (polymers) in Australia.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.

and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and other
information available to it.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The market share aggregation in the supply of bulk containerised
logistics to customers requiring services for plastics customers
in Australia, as a result of the Acquisition, is estimated to be low.
• The merged entity would continue to face competition from
alternative suppliers of bulk containerised logistics, including to
customers requiring logistics services for plastics in Australia.

days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_table_content.details:
Protech Group (Aust) Pty Ltd (Protech) proposed acquisition of
100% of the shares of ActivateRail Pty Ltd (ActivateRail) (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Protech, is an Australian based labour hire provider to
technical industries including renewables, building and construction,
civil construction and infrastructure, industrial maintenance and
engineering, mining and resources, traffic management, rail
operations, asphalt and road surfacing, warehousing and
manufacturing and defence. Quantum Safety Pty Ltd (Quantum
Safety), a wholly owned subsidiary of Protech, supplies rail safety
and site management and supervision services in New South Wales
and Queensland.
The target, ActivateRail, supplies rail safety and site management
and supervision services to utilities, engineering and professional
service organisations, primarily in Victoria.

Protech, through Quantum Safety, and ActivateRail (the Parties)
overlap in the supply of rail safety and site management and
supervision services in New South Wales and Queensland.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, publicly available information and information
from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Quantum Safety and ActivateRail do not appear to be close
competitors.
• The merged firm would likely continue to face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers of rail safety and site management
and supervision services.
The ACCC also received concerns regarding Protech’s ability to

branded site. Following the Acquisition, bp Gateway is intended to be
operated by bp as a company owned and operated site.

Tamworth and Port Macquarie.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Endeavour Purchaser V, Inc, an affiliate of various funds advised
and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (Blackstone) applied
for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of
100% of the equity interests in Dresser Utility Solutions, LLC
(Dresser), as described in the transaction documents provided as
part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
25 August 2026

The acquirer, Blackstone, is a US-based corporation, incorporated
under the laws of Delaware, United States. Blackstone operates as
an investment management firm, not as a conglomerate or holding
company. Accordingly, each company in its investment portfolio is
independently managed and financed and each has different
investors (although the investors in different investment funds may
overlap). Each Blackstone portfolio company has its own board of
directors, which generally also include Blackstone representatives.
The target, Dresser, is a US-based company that manufactures and
supplies equipment used globally to build, operate and repair gas
and water utility networks.
In Australia, Dresser supplies gas meters, gas regulators and
couplings & clamp products, both directly and through third-party
distributors.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. There is no horizontal overlap or vertical
relationship between Blackstone or its controlled portfolio
companies and Dresser in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
Australian Retirement Trust Pty Ltd as trustee for Australian
Retirement Trust (ART) (via wholly owned investment vehicles
managed by QIC Limited and/or its related bodies corporate (QIC))
propose to acquire a 50% interest in the Westfield Mt Gravatt
shopping centre (the Property) (together with interests in certain
ancillary and incidental non-rental income streams in connection
with and derived from the ownership of the Property, the Target), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the

25 August 2026

The acquirer, ART, is an Australian superannuation fund that has
invested over $350 billion in retirement savings for more than
2.4 million members (as at 30 June 2025). ART has limited minority
interests in a small number of shopping and retail centres in
Queensland, including in the Brisbane area.
QIC is an Australian institutional investment manager established in
1991 by the Queensland Government. QIC specialises in alternative
asset classes including infrastructure, real estate, private equity,
private debt, natural capital, and liquid markets, serving both
government and non-government institutional clients. As of 30 June
2025, QIC managed approximately $137 billion in assets under
management.
Scentre Group is an ASX-listed Australian stapled group established
in 2014 following its demerger from Westfield Group. Scentre owns,
develops and manages a portfolio of 42 Westfield shopping centres
across Australia and New Zealand, including Westfield Mt Gravatt.
Its business encompasses property investment, development,
design, construction, leasing and asset management.
The Target consists of 50% interest in the Property and certain
associated non-rental income streams derived from Westfield Mt
Gravatt, a large shopping centre in Mt Gravatt, Brisbane. Westfield

Brisbane area
b. there are alternative shopping and retail centres in south-
east metropolitan Brisbane
c. any increment to ART’s shares of revenue in the supply of
out-of-home advertising opportunities, gift cards, and
ancillary and incidental shopping centre services is low
d. there are alternative suppliers of advertising opportunities,
gift cards, and shopping centre ancillary services.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the

competition.

determination_table_content.details:
Little Company of Mary Health Care Ltd (Calvary) proposes to
acquire the business and assets of Hobart Private Hospital (Hobart

agreement (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has

Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Calvary, is a not-for-profit operator of public and private
hospitals in Australia, present in New South Wales, South Australia,
Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory. Calvary currently
operates four private hospitals in Tasmania: St Vincent's Hospital
(Launceston); St Luke's Hospital (Launceston); Lenah Valley
Hospital (Lenah Valley, Hobart); and St John's Hospital (South
Hobart).
The target, Hobart Private, is a private hospital co-located with and
adjacent to Hobart's main public hospital, Royal Hobart Hospital.
Hobart Private is currently operated by Healthscope, a private
hospital operator. In May 2025, Healthscope’s parent entities went
into voluntary administration, and receivers and administrators were
appointed by its lenders and the Healthscope Board, respectively, to
conduct an orderly sale of the hospitals in its network.
The reasons for the ACCC’s determination are set out in section 2.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines.

In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered the information and documents that were submitted with the notification form, additional information provided by the parties to the Acquisition, information and submissions received from third parties, publicly available information and other information available to it.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect.
Overlap between the Parties

Calvary (through its Lenah Valley Hospital and St John’s Hospital) and Hobart Private overlap in the supply of private hospital services in the area surrounding Hobart Private. This includes the supply of medical, surgical and emergency care services across a range of medical specialties. Calvary and Hobart Private both provide private hospital services for day procedures, as well as procedures which require an overnight hospital stay.
Industry background
Private hospital services

Certain medical procedures are generally only conducted in hospitals which have facilities for overnight hospital stays. Overnight hospitals generally have more advanced facilities and infrastructure, which are particularly important for the provision of acute medical procedures. Other medical procedures, generally being less complex procedures, may be provided at either overnight hospitals or day hospitals.

There are three major private hospitals in Hobart that offer overnight services, two of which are operated by Calvary and one of which is currently operated by Healthscope: a) Lenah Valley Hospital is Calvary’s larger, higher severity private hospital in Hobart, providing complex surgical, emergency, maternity and specialist inpatient services. Lenah Valley Hospital has 178 beds, an intensive care unit, a 24/7 emergency department, an endoscopy suite and 9 operating theatres; b) St John’s Hospital, also operated by Calvary, provides a more limited range of services relative to Lenah Valley Hospital, focusing on lower severity and short stay surgical procedures, select medical services and procedural activity. St John’s Hospital has 104 beds and 4 operating theatres; c) Hobart Private, currently operated by Healthscope, offers healthcare services including medical and surgical services and emergency care. Hobart Private’s surgical program covers general, specialist and sub-specialty surgical procedures. General medical services delivered at Hobart Private include cardiology, gastroenterology, neurology, renal and respiratory medicine. Hobart Private has 133 beds and 9 operating theatres, and operates a 24/7 emergency department.

In addition to the hospitals listed above, private mental health services are provided at the Hobart Clinic, a 27-bed inpatient facility located in Rokeby. The Hobart Clinic only accepts referrals for admissions on a case-by-case basis.

Hobart also has four main private day hospitals which offer a more limited range of medical procedures, treatment and surgery which are delivered on a same-day basis (that is, they do not offer procedures which require an overnight hospital stay): a) Nexus Hobart Day Surgery, which provides services including ophthalmology, plastic surgery, oral & maxillofacial surgery, dental surgery, paediatric surgery, urology, vasectomy and certain in vitro fertilisation (IVF) services; b) Virtus Hobart Specialist Day Hospital, which is a Hobart-based day surgery that provides services including gastroenterology, endoscopy, gynaecology, fertility and IVF, ophthalmology, orthopaedic, urology and general surgery services; c) Icon Cancer Care Centre, which provides services including medical and radiation oncology services in central Hobart; and d) Hobart Eye Surgeons, which provides a range of ophthalmology services through four locations around Hobart.
Public hospital services

Royal Hobart Hospital is Tasmania’s largest public hospital and major referral centre. It provides a comprehensive range of general, specialty medical and surgical services including cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, extensive burns treatment, hyperbaric medicine, maternity care and gynaecology, neonatal and paediatric intensive care, as well as high-risk obstetrics services. Royal Hobart Hospital has approximately 500 beds and operates a 24/7 emergency department, a 24/7 intensive care unit and a high dependency unit.
Calvary’s service offering

Calvary operates in accordance with the Code of Ethical Standards for Catholic Health and Aged Care Services in Australia (Catholic Code). This means that certain services are generally not offered at Calvary’s facilities, including IVF and other assisted reproductive services, voluntary assisted dying, elective terminations of pregnancy, and gender reassignment procedures.
Competition assessment

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed.
Relevant areas of competition

The ACCC has considered whether the Acquisition is likely to substantially lessen competition in the supply of private hospital services in the area surrounding Hobart Private. For the purpose of its assessment, it was not necessary to reach a definitive view on the precise product or geographic boundaries of the relevant market, as it does not materially alter the ACCC’s competition assessment.
Competition effects in the supply of private hospital services
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the supply of private hospital services in the area surrounding Hobart Private.

As noted above, the ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed. This comparative exercise is a tool of analysis to assist the ACCC in assessing whether the Acquisition is likely to result in a substantial lessening of competition. The ACCC’s consideration of the likely future state of competition without the Acquisition has been a central focus of its assessment of the Acquisition.

Based on the materials before it, the ACCC makes the following findings: a) there is not a real commercial likelihood of an alternative purchaser acquiring Hobart Private; b) in the absence of a commercially realistic alternative purchaser, and in the context of Healthscope’s voluntary administration, there is a real prospect that Hobart Private would cease operating as a private hospital in the future without the Acquisition; c) Calvary would be the sole major private hospital offering overnight services in Hobart following the Acquisition.

The ACCC considers that there would be a material reduction in the number of suppliers of private hospital services, including day services, in the area surrounding Hobart Private in both the future with and without the Acquisition. Accordingly, the ACCC considers that the future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds is unlikely to be substantially less than the future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed.

The ACCC has had regard to feedback received from several third parties (including medical practitioners and industry bodies) regarding certain services currently provided at Hobart Private, which Calvary would likely not provide if the Acquisition proceeds, given that Calvary operates in accordance with the Catholic Code. The services that would likely not be provided by Calvary at Hobart Private if the Acquisition proceeds include certain IVF and other assisted reproductive services, voluntary assisted dying, elective terminations of pregnancy, and gender reassignment procedures.

Having regard to all the material currently before it, the ACCC considers that these particular private hospital services would likely cease being provided at Hobart Private in both the future with and without the Acquisition.

(OT) cybersecurity asset discovery, vulnerability management and
threat detection technology, as well as threat intelligence and related
services. Its subsidiary, Phosphorus, provides extended Internet of
Things (xIoT) device discovery, vulnerability identification and
remediation technology. Dragos is headquartered in the US.

and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.

notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.

the information and documents that were submitted with the

proposed acquisition of 100% of the shares in runZero, Inc (MN-

supply of OT cybersecurity services in Australia;
• post-Acquisition, Accenture would continue to face competition

determination_table_content.details:
The Parties overlap horizontally in the supply of data collaboration

data collaboration services are an input into the supply of
advertising services.

and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an

the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information obtained from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Publicis and LiveRamp are not close competitors in the supply of
data ingestion and unification services and Publicis does not
supply data clean room services.
• Publicis would be unlikely to have the ability and incentive to
foreclose rival providers of advertising services. In considering
Publicis’ ability and incentive post-acquisition, the ACCC had
regard to third party feedback that LiveRamp’s strength in the
supply of data ingestion and unification services globally meant

services. However, the ACCC considered the position of
LiveRamp in Australia and found that there were alternative
suppliers of data ingestion and unification services available to
advertisers and advertising agencies in Australia.
• Publicis would be unlikely to have the ability and incentive to
foreclose rival advertising service providers, for example by
denying or degrading their access to LiveRamp’s data
cleanroom services, as there are alternative suppliers of data
clean room services in Australia.

the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_table_content.details:
Newco, an entity to be established by Verlinvest SA (Verlinvest),
proposes to acquire up to approximately 60% of the shares of
Tukazza ! SAS (Tukazza), as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
Newco and Verlinvest applied for a notification waiver in respect of
the Acquisition.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
28 August 2026

The acquirer, Newco, is a société par actions simplifiée to be
established by Verlinvest for the purposes of the Acquisition.
Verlinvest is an international evergreen investment company
headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. Verlinvest focuses on investing
in high-growth brands within the food, beverage and fast-moving
consumer goods, health, consumer technology and lifestyle sectors.
The firm has over EUR 2 billion in assets under management and
operates offices in Brussels, New York, London, Mumbai, and
Singapore.
The target, Tukazza, is the holding company of the HomeExchange
group (HomeExchange). HomeExchange is a global private
accommodation online travel agency that offers online
intermediation services that allow members to exchange homes for
holidays and travel.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal or vertical
overlap between Verlinvest (including its connected entities) and
HomeExchange in the supply of online intermediary services for
private accommodation in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
GTown Motors Pty Ltd (GTown Motors) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of a motor vehicle
dealership business located in Grafton NSW known as Grafton
Mazda, as described in the transaction documents provided as part
of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) not to make the notification waiver
determination applied for.
27 August 2026

The acquirer, GTown Motors, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Grafton
Motor Group Pty Ltd (GMG). Houma Holdings Pty Ltd (Houma) is a
majority (80%) shareholder of the shares in GMG. The remaining
20% are owned by Robert John Connell, an unrelated third party.
Houma is the majority shareholder of several new and use motor
vehicle dealerships within NSW and QLD.
GMG operates a new and used motor vehicle dealership in Grafton
NSW known as Grafton Motors. The dealership represents 3 vehicle
brands, being Toyota, Suzuki and Hyundai.
The target, Grafton Mazda, is operated by Ken Casson Motors Pty
Ltd (Ken Casson Motors), and supplies new Mazda vehicles, as well
as used motor vehicles. Ken Casson Motors also has an
arrangement with Holden Australia for the supply of Holden parts.
Both GMG and Grafton Mazda supply new and used cars, spare
parts, car servicing and repair services, and finance.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, including the
acquirer’s (and its connected entities) revenues in Australia, the
ACCC considers it is likely that, if the Acquisition were put into
effect, the notification thresholds would be met.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not
be likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information provided, given:
a. the Acquisition would combine the largest dealership of
new and used cars in the local Grafton region of NSW
with one of only two other new and used car dealerships
in that region
b. the merged entity’s combined share of supply of new
and used cars in the Grafton region of NSW may be
significant
c. there is uncertainty regarding the extent to which the
merged entity would be likely to face intra-brand and
inter-brand competition from alternative dealerships in
the Grafton region and the surrounding areas more
broadly.
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition warrants consideration
through the notification process, including further information
gathering and consultation with third parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
Monadelphous Group Limited (Monadelphous) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the issued share capital of Tyden Power Pty Ltd (Tyden Power), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) not to make the notification waiver
determination applied for.
27 August 2026

The acquirer, Monadelphous, is an ASX-listed Australian engineering
group providing construction, maintenance, and industrial services to
the resources, energy, and infrastructure sectors. Its offering
includes engineering, construction and maintenance services for
electricity infrastructure (electrical infrastructure services).
The target, Tyden Power, is a New South Wales-based provider of
services for the full lifecycle of high-voltage electrical assets,
delivering services to customers in the energy, utilities, and
infrastructure sectors, including electrical infrastructure services. Its
capabilities include transmission and distribution infrastructure,
substations, protection and control systems, asset inspections, and
network upgrades.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not be
likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information currently before it. In particular:
a. there is horizontal overlap between Monadelphous and
Tyden Power in the supply of electrical infrastructure
services in Australia
b. the extent to which Monadelphous is likely to be constrained
by alternative suppliers of electrical infrastructure services
post-acquisition, either nationally or on a state-wide (or
narrower) basis, is uncertain
c. the parties’ combined share of the national and/or state-
based supply of electrical infrastructure services and the
increment arising from the Acquisition is unclear.
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition warrants consideration
through the notification process, including via consultation with third
parties.
Based on the information provided in the application, including the
parties’ revenues in Australia, the ACCC considers that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds would be
met.
For these reasons, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
